component: LLM brain — low-latency, in-character English debate partner running locally on M5 Max 128GB (replacing VoxEMW's deepseek-v4-flash API call)
recommendation: Primary: **Hermes-4.3-36B at 4-bit MLX** (`leonsarmiento/Hermes-4.3-36B-4bit-mlx`, ~21 GB), served by `mlx_lm.server` (mlx-lm >= 0.28.3) on 127.0.0.1:8080, and wired into VoxEMW by KEEPING `llm.backend: chat-completions` and changing only `base_url` to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1`. Do NOT switch to `llm.backend: mlx-lm` (see evidence — it drops sentence batching and clears the KV cache every turn). Add a session-start pre-warm request so the 2000-token persona prefix is already cached before the first utterance. Upgrade path if quality disappoints: `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B` 4-bit (69.6 GB, measured 65.9 tok/s / 881 t/s prefill on this exact chip) — it also fits, with the caveat that its Gated-DeltaNet hybrid layers make prefix-cache reuse fragile.
why:
Three findings drive this.

(1) **The author's "local 8B not good enough" conclusion does not transfer, and neither does his model.** DeepSeek-V4-Flash is 284B total / 13B active, MIT, open weights. But the arithmetic kills it: 284B x 4 bits = 142 GB, x 4.25 (MXFP4 incl. scales) = 151 GB, x ~3.3 (real 3-bit) = 117 GB — all above the ~96-115 GB the GPU can actually wire on a 128 GB Mac. The only quant that fits is 2.44 bpw (92.8 GB disk / 84.4 GB peak), and someone has already benchmarked exactly that on an M5 Max 128GB: 36.1 tok/s decode, 498 t/s prefill, **TTFT 2055 ms at a 1k prompt** — over your entire 2.0 s budget before STT or TTS get a turn. It also loses 7.3 points of MMLU-Pro versus the API, and needs oMLX because `deepseek_v4` is still unsupported in mainline mlx-lm (issue #1281, open). So: the exact model he used is the *worst* local option here.

(2) **Latency is decided by prefix caching, not by tokens/sec.** Your prompt is ~2000 persona tokens + ~30 turns (~3,600 tokens) ≈ 5,600 tokens. Cold TTFT = 5600 / prefill_rate: 4.2 s for gpt-oss-120b, 6.4 s for Qwen3.5-122B, 8 s for Hermes-36B, 11 s for DeepSeek-V4-Flash. **Every candidate blows the budget cold.** Warm, only the new user turn (~40 tokens) is prefilled — 0.03-0.08 s — and time-to-first-*sentence* becomes ~18 tokens / decode_rate. That is 0.72 s for Hermes-4.3-36B-4bit, 0.27 s for Qwen3.5-122B, 0.20 s for gpt-oss-120b. End to end (VAD 0.1 + STT 0.4 + LLM + VoxCPM2/Qwen3-TTS TTFA 0.3): **~1.65 s for Hermes, ~1.2 s for the two big MoEs — all inside 2.0 s, but only with a warm cache.** Hence: pre-warm at persona load, and keep the history append-only (see risks re: `chat_size: 30`).

(3) **Persona adherence is the binding constraint, and only one model family has published evidence on it.** The Hermes 4 technical report built RefusalBench (166 hand-written prompts, 32 categories, three inverted for genuine-harm categories; higher = fewer refusals) and reports Hermes 4 57.1 vs Grok 4 51.3, DeepSeek V3 28.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro 24.2, Llama 3.1 405B 21.7, GPT-4o 17.7, Sonnet 4 17.0. Its qualitative section names exactly your failure mode — most models show *"policy rigidity... a tendency to foreground policy compliance even when faced with clearly fictional or controlled prompts"* — and reports Hermes *"generated in-character responses without repeated disclaimers"* and *"more closely embodied the requested persona"*, including on political-analysis prompts. Hermes 4.3 claims RefusalBench SOTA among non-abliterated models (74.60% answered). Against that, gpt-oss-120b — the fastest option — is the one model with documented over-refusal on *political analysis* specifically, plus an instruction hierarchy where system-level safety instructions are designed to outrank the developer/persona prompt. That is architecturally hostile to a persona that must argue a contested position, so it is disqualified as primary despite being the speed winner.

Hermes-4.3-36B is dense (ByteDance Seed-OSS-36B base) with ordinary full GQA attention, which is also why its prefix cache reuse is clean in mlx-lm while gpt-oss (sliding window) and Qwen3.5 (SSM/GDN) are the two named-broken cases in issue #980. It costs you decode speed (~25 vs ~88 tok/s) but buys the two things you actually cannot compromise on, and at 21 GB it leaves ~90 GB free for STT, TTS, the VLM sidecar, and headroom to A/B a 122B against it in the same session. Your persona is also in English, not Chinese — a materially easier target than the Chinese persona work that produced the original "8B inadequate" verdict.

evidence.claim: DeepSeek-V4-Flash is 284B total / 13B active, MIT-licensed, open weights, 1M context, hybrid thinking with a Non-think mode; native dtype is FP4 experts + FP8 elsewhere
evidence.detail: Official model card. Confirms V4-Flash is the 284B/13B-active sibling of the 1.6T/49B-active V4-Pro, released under MIT. Hybrid attention = Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) + Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA), stated at ~10% of DeepSeek-V3.2's KV cache. Thinking cannot be removed but 'Non-think' mode is selectable — this is the open-weights equivalent of the reasoning_effort: none the VoxEMW config already sets.

evidence.claim: The only DeepSeek-V4-Flash quant that fits 128 GB has a measured TTFT of 2055 ms at a 1k prompt on an M5 Max 128GB — already over the whole 2.0 s budget
evidence.detail: Model card benchmarks are run on exactly our target hardware (M5 Max 128GB, 40-core GPU): 92.8 GB on disk / 86.5 GiB, 2.44 bits per weight, 84.4 GB peak memory. Generation 36.1 tok/s at 1k falling to 31.5 tok/s at 32k; prefill 498.3 tok/s at 1k; TTFT 2055 ms at 1k and 97,347 ms at 32k. MMLU-Pro 0.573 vs 0.647 for the full-precision API (~7.3 points lost). Requires oMLX 0.5.7+, explicitly 'cannot run on standard mlx-lm'.

evidence.claim: mlx-lm mainline still does not implement the deepseek_v4 architecture
evidence.detail: Issue open as of filing (May 2026); mlx-lm supports DeepSeek V2/V3 only. CSA and HCA both need new implementations. Confirmed from the other direction by the mlx-lm source: seed_oss, gpt_oss, qwen3_next, glm4_moe, deepseek_v3, minimax and Kimi K2.5 are all present in mlx_lm/models, but no deepseek_v4.

evidence.claim: Prefix cache reuse in mlx-lm is broken for exactly the architectures of the fastest candidates — and works for plain full-attention models
evidence.detail: Open issue (filed 2026-03-11), PRs unmerged. Confirmed broken: sliding-window attention (gpt-oss-120b, Gemma 3), SSM/Mamba layers (Qwen 3.5, all sizes), mixed attention (Qwen2.5-VL), iRoPE (Llama 4 Scout/Maverick). Confirmed working: MiniMax M2.5 (pure full attention + MoE). Root causes: RotatingKVCache cannot be trimmed to a prefix boundary, and SSM recurrent state is not splittable at token boundaries. Measured on M3 Ultra: MiniMax 29.3 s -> 2.79 s (10.5x); gpt-oss/Qwen3.5 no improvement, some requests slower. Hermes-4.3-36B is dense Seed-OSS with ordinary GQA, so it lands on the working side.

evidence.claim: Measured M5 Max prefill and decode rates for the large MoE candidates (mlx_lm)
evidence.detail: gpt-oss-120B (64 GB): 1,325 t/s prompt + 87.9 t/s gen at 4K; 2,537 t/s + 64.5 t/s at 32K. Qwen3.5-122B-A10B 4-bit (69.6 GB): 881 t/s + 65.9 t/s at 4K; 1,068 t/s + 54.9 t/s at 32K. Qwen3-Coder-Next 8-bit (84.7 GB): 754 t/s + 79.3 t/s at 4K. Qwen3.5-27B 6-bit (26 GB): 811 t/s + 23.6 t/s at 4K. The last row is the anchor for estimating dense Hermes-4.3-36B. Note these contradict presenc.ai's '14-19 tps for gpt-oss-120b on M5 Max', which appears to treat a 5.1B-active MoE as dense — discard that source.

evidence.claim: Hermes 4 is the only candidate with published evidence on refusal rate AND on staying in character without disclaimers
evidence.detail: Hermes 4 Technical Report, extracted from the PDF directly. RefusalBench (166 prompts, 32 categories, 3 inverted for minor-harm/trafficking/self-harm; Sonnet 4 as judge; higher = fewer refusals): Hermes 4 Reasoning 57.1, Grok 4 51.3, Hermes 4 Non-reasoning 43.2, DeepSeek V3 28.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro 24.23, Llama 3.1 405B 21.7, Gemini 2.5 Flash 19.13, GPT-4o 17.67, Sonnet 4 17. The 14B table shows 59.5/49.0. Section 5 verbatim: most models exhibit 'policy rigidity... a tendency to foreground policy compliance even when faced with clearly fictional or controlled prompts'; Hermes 4 'generated in-character responses without repeated disclaimers' and 'more closely embodied the requested persona'; 'responses are more readily shaped by system-level cues... enabling consistent persona embodiment and reduced sycophancy when explicitly instructed.' Political-analysis prompts are one of the five probed genres.

evidence.claim: Hermes-4.3-36B is dense 36B on ByteDance Seed-OSS-36B-Base, Apache 2.0, with a thinking toggle and RefusalBench SOTA among non-abliterated models
evidence.detail: Dense (not MoE), 36B, Apache 2.0, context extended to 512K, claims 74.60% of RefusalBench questions answered — 'SOTA across non-abliterated models'. Reasoning is opt-in via a reasoning system prompt / thinking=True; omitting it disables <think> blocks entirely, which is exactly what you need (VoxEMW's whole reason for reasoning_effort: none was the ~2 s think delay before speaking). Recommended sampling temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, top_k=20. Nous frames the post-training as 'neutral alignment' — no political or moral stance baked in.

evidence.claim: Hermes-4.3-36B MLX quants already exist at 4/5/6/8-bit and mlx-lm supports the seed_oss architecture
evidence.detail: Converted with mlx-lm 0.28.3 — proof seed_oss loads in mainline mlx-lm, no port needed. 4-bit uses mixed quantization (6-bit embeddings/lm_head, 4-bit elsewhere), ~21 GB. Siblings: leonsarmiento/...-6bit-mlx (~29 GB), lukaskremla/Hermes-4.3-36B-mlx-5Bit, alexcovo/Hermes-4.3-36B-mlx-8Bit (~38 GB). Independently confirmed against mlx-lm's model registry, which lists seed_oss in its test configurations.

evidence.claim: gpt-oss-120b — the fastest candidate — has documented over-refusal on political analysis and a safety hierarchy designed to outrank the persona prompt
evidence.detail: User reports of refusals triggered on political analysis, creative writing and psychological analysis. Separately, the 120b's wider expert router is described as creating a broader safety surface than 20b's, giving higher residual refusal, and openai/harmony issue #80 notes the model often emits refusals outside the harmony channel structure (a parsing hazard for any streaming pipeline). The gpt-oss model card's instruction-hierarchy evaluations establish that system-level safety instructions take precedence over developer/user content — structurally the opposite of what a persona override needs.

evidence.claim: VoxEMW's own args.py silently drops sentence batching and history size when llm.backend is set to mlx-lm
evidence.detail: Lines 76-85: --chat_size (76-77), --stream_batch_sentences (78-79) and --responses_api_reasoning_effort (80-81) are all rendered inside the `if backend in ("chat-completions", "responses-api")` block. The `elif backend == "mlx-lm"` branch at line 82 adds only --llm_device. So flipping the config to mlx-lm loses stream_batch_sentences: 1 — the setting the whole voice pipeline's TTFA depends on — and falls back to the upstream default. This is the concrete reason to keep chat-completions and point base_url at a local server instead of switching backends.

evidence.claim: The upstream speech-to-speech mlx-lm backend calls mx.clear_cache() after each generation, so no KV cache survives between turns
evidence.detail: LanguageModelHandler._generate uses mlx_stream_generate and _stream_tokens does batch into sentences honouring stream_batch_sentences — but mx.clear_cache() after generation means the cache is not persistently reused across turns. With a 2000-token persona plus 30 turns of history that means a full ~5,600-token re-prefill every single turn. By contrast the chat-completions path (BaseOpenAICompatibleHandler._consume_streaming, nltk.sent_tokenize + stream_batch_sentences) talks to an external server that CAN hold an LRU prefix cache. This is the decisive argument for the OpenAI-compatible local-server topology.

evidence.claim: mlx_lm.server implements a trie-backed LRU prefix cache across requests
evidence.detail: ResponseGenerator in mlx_lm/server.py calls fetch_nearest_cache against an LRUPromptCache backed by a PromptTrie; on a prefix match only the remaining tokens are prefilled, and the post-generation cache (including newly generated tokens) is inserted back. Crucially the failure mode in issue #980 is *trimming* — needed only when the new prompt is SHORTER than the cached one. In an append-only voice conversation the prompt grows monotonically, so reuse works even for hybrid architectures; the break happens when chat_size rolls the window and drops the oldest turns.

evidence.claim: M5 Max hardware ceiling: 614 GB/s unified memory bandwidth, 40-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in every core
evidence.detail: 614 GB/s (up from 546 GB/s on M4 Max), up to 128 GB unified memory, 18-core CPU + up to 40-core GPU. The per-core Neural Accelerators are matmul units sharing the same memory path — they are why prompt processing is reported 35-40% faster than M4 Max, which is the half of the latency equation that matters for a 2000-token persona prefix. Verified locally: hw.memsize = 137438953472 (128 GiB); iogpu.wired_limit_mb currently 0, i.e. macOS default of roughly 75% (~96 GB) available to the GPU unless raised.

evidence.claim: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B is Apache 2.0, 122B/10B-active, 262K context, hybrid Gated DeltaNet + attention, thinking-on by default
evidence.detail: 48 layers, 256 experts (8 routed + 1 shared), Gated Attention 32 Q-heads / 2 KV-heads / 256-dim, Gated DeltaNet 64 V-heads / 16 QK-heads. Roughly 75% of layers are linear-attention, so the KV cache is tiny (~24 KB/token) but prefix-cache reuse is the SSM case broken in mlx-lm issue #980. Thinking is ON by default and must be disabled with chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false} — miss this and you reintroduce exactly the ~2 s pre-speech delay VoxEMW's reasoning_effort: none was added to kill. Non-thinking sampling: temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, presence_penalty=1.5.

evidence.claim: Everything larger than ~230B is out of reach on 128 GB, so the shortlist really is this short
evidence.detail: Mistral Large 3 is 675B/41B-active (Apache 2.0) — 2-bit would still be ~169 GB. Kimi K3 is 2.8T/104B-active and needs 1.6 TB+ aggregate; Kimi K2.5 is 1T/32B-active (~250 GB at 2-bit). Command A is 111B DENSE under CC-BY-NC (non-commercial) and would decode at roughly 5-6 tok/s here. GLM-4.7 is 355B/32B-active MIT — ~133 GB even at 3-bit. MiniMax-M2.5 (230B/10B, MIT, all 62 layers full GQA) is the one big model whose prefix cache provably works, but 4-bit is ~115 GB (too tight beside STT/TTS) and 3-bit ~86 GB.

alternatives.name: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, 4-bit MLX (69.6 GB) — the quality upgrade
alternatives.tradeoff: Best quality-per-GB that fits: measured 65.9 tok/s decode and 881 t/s prefill on an M5 Max, Apache 2.0, 262K context, and ~2.6x faster to first sentence than Hermes-36B. Costs: (a) hybrid Gated-DeltaNet layers are a named-broken case for mlx-lm prefix-cache trimming, so a rolled history window means a full ~6.4 s re-prefill instead of a cheap trim; (b) thinking is ON by default and must be explicitly disabled; (c) 70 GB leaves only ~25 GB for STT + TTS + VLM + OS; (d) no published persona/refusal evidence — Chinese-model refusal patterns are documented mainly for China-sensitive topics, not Western gender politics, so this is an unknown you have to test rather than a known risk.
alternatives.when_to_prefer: Prefer as soon as Hermes-4.3-36B's arguments feel thin or repetitive in real debate — that is the specific failure this fixes. Also prefer if you drop the MiniCPM-V vision sidecar and free its memory. Run it with a large chat_size and compact_history off so the prefix never needs trimming.

alternatives.name: gpt-oss-120b, native MXFP4 (~63 GB) — the speed ceiling
alternatives.tradeoff: Fastest large model on this chip by a wide margin: 1,325 t/s prefill and 87.9 tok/s decode at 4K, rising to 2,710 t/s prefill at 16K, in only 63 GB. Time to first sentence would be ~0.35 s end-of-LLM. But it is the single worst fit for criterion 5: documented over-refusal specifically on political analysis, a 128-expert router described as giving higher residual refusal than the 20b, an instruction hierarchy engineered so system-level safety outranks the developer/persona prompt, and a harmony-template bug where refusals are emitted outside the expected channel structure (which would confuse the sentence-splitter feeding TTS). Sliding-window attention also puts it on the broken side of mlx-lm issue #980.
alternatives.when_to_prefer: Only if you re-scope the persona to something non-contentious, or if you are willing to run a Heretic/abliterated derivative — and note that abliteration is reported to cost stability on odd prompts, which in a live voice loop shows up as incoherence rather than a clean refusal. Do not start here.

alternatives.name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash 2.4bit-mixed via oMLX (84.4 GB peak) — the literal answer to "DeepSeek v4 locally"
alternatives.tradeoff: It is genuinely the model the user asked for, MIT-licensed, and it does fit. But it fails the product: 2055 ms TTFT at a 1k prompt (~11 s at your real ~5,600-token prompt, cold), 36.1 tok/s decode, 7.3 MMLU-Pro points lost to the quantization, and it requires oMLX 0.5.7+ because mainline mlx-lm has no deepseek_v4 implementation — a non-mainline runtime dependency in the middle of your critical path. It also eats 84 GB, crowding out the rest of the pipeline.
alternatives.when_to_prefer: Only for offline/batch work, or as a curiosity benchmark to see how close 2.44 bpw gets to the API you are replacing. Not for the real-time loop. If you want DeepSeek V4's actual quality, use the API (below), not this quant.

alternatives.name: MiniMax-M2.5, 3-bit MLX (~86 GB) — the cache-safe big model
alternatives.tradeoff: 230B/10B-active, MIT, and the one large MoE explicitly confirmed WORKING in mlx-lm issue #980 (all 62 layers are plain full GQA), where it showed a 10.5x TTFT speedup from prefix reuse on an M3 Ultra. That makes its latency behaviour predictable in a way Qwen3.5's is not. Downsides: 4-bit (~115 GB) does not leave room for the rest of the pipeline so you are forced to 3-bit with the attendant quality loss; it is tuned for coding/agentic work rather than conversation; and no persona/refusal evidence exists for it.
alternatives.when_to_prefer: If you try Qwen3.5-122B and find the rolling-window re-prefill stalls are what actually break the experience, this is the same weight class with the cache problem designed out.

alternatives.name: Keep the deepseek-v4-flash API brain (zero code change)
alternatives.tradeoff: Highest raw quality, zero memory cost, and already working — the config sets reasoning_effort: "none" to suppress the ~2 s thinking delay. But it adds network RTT to every single turn (the author measured ~0.6 s for the DeepSeek call), leaks every word of a politically sensitive conversation to a third party, costs per token, breaks offline, and is subject to provider-side content filtering that can make the persona refuse in ways you cannot fix. Note DeepSeek's own reasoning_effort levels on the 0731 variant are low/high/max, so "none" depends on the provider honouring the non-think mode.
alternatives.when_to_prefer: Keep it as a one-line fallback, not a plan. Because the recommendation keeps llm.backend: chat-completions, switching between local and API is literally editing base_url + api_key_env — so run both and A/B the persona quality directly. Worth it only if BOTH Hermes-4.3-36B and Qwen3.5-122B fail the in-character test, which the RefusalBench evidence suggests is unlikely.

alternatives.name: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B / Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 4-bit (~20 GB) — the latency insurance policy
alternatives.tradeoff: 3B active params means very high decode (a 30B-A3B is reported at 58 tok/s on M5 Max) in ~20 GB, so time-to-first-sentence would be ~0.3 s. But 3B active is thin for sustained argumentation — this is the size class closest to the '8B brain was inadequate' verdict, just with better routing.
alternatives.when_to_prefer: If measured end-to-end latency turns out worse than modelled (e.g. STT is slower than 0.4 s, or TTS TTFA drifts up) and you need to claw back 0.5 s from the LLM stage. Also a good smoke-test model to validate the whole local-server wiring before downloading 21-70 GB.

latency_estimate:
**Hermes-4.3-36B-4bit, warm cache: ~0.85 s from end-of-speech-to-text to first complete sentence handed to TTS; ~1.6 s end-to-end to first audio out.** Inside the 2.0 s target, comfortably inside the 3.0 s ceiling.

Model (all rates measured on M5 Max unless noted):
- TTFT_warm = new_tokens / prefill_rate + server overhead. Only the new user turn (~40 tok) is prefilled: 40 / ~700 t/s = 0.06 s, plus ~50-150 ms HTTP + tokenize + sampler setup ≈ **0.1-0.2 s**.
- Time-to-first-sentence = TTFT + sentence_tokens / decode_rate. A spoken first sentence is ~18 tokens. Hermes-4.3-36B 4-bit decodes at ~24-30 tok/s (extrapolated from the measured Qwen3.5-27B-6bit anchor of 23.6 tok/s at 26 GB, scaled by weight bytes at ~85% bandwidth efficiency on 614 GB/s): 18 / 25 = **0.72 s**. Total LLM stage ≈ **0.85 s**.
- End to end: VAD/SmartTurn ~0.1 s + Qwen3-ASR-0.6B 0.3-0.5 s (author's measured 0.3-1.0 s for 2-5 s utterances) + LLM 0.85 s + Qwen3-TTS TTFA ~0.3 s ≈ **1.55-1.75 s**.

For comparison, same math warm: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-4bit 18/65.9 = 0.27 s -> ~1.2 s end-to-end; gpt-oss-120b 18/87.9 = 0.20 s -> ~1.15 s; DeepSeek-V4-Flash-2.4bit 18/36.1 = 0.50 s -> ~1.4 s (but see cold, below).

**COLD is the number that matters and it fails for everything.** With a 2000-token persona + 30 turns (~120 tok/turn) ≈ 5,600 tokens and no cache: Hermes-36B 5600/~700 = **8.0 s**; gpt-oss-120b 5600/1325 = 4.2 s; Qwen3.5-122B 5600/881 = 6.4 s; DeepSeek-V4-Flash 5600/498 = 11.2 s. So the pre-warm is not an optimization, it is a requirement: issue one throwaway completion carrying the persona system prompt at `Session._apply_persona()` (voxemw/gateway/orchestrator.py:343-347, where the persona text is already being injected via session.update), before the user's first utterance. That converts turn 1 from an 8 s stall into a normal turn.

Second-order effects: decode at 25 tok/s ≈ 1,100 wpm against ~150 wpm of speech, so once the first sentence lands the LLM stays far ahead of playback — `stream_batch_sentences: 1` means only the FIRST sentence is on the critical path, and everything after is hidden behind audio. Growth over a session is mild: by turn 30 the prompt is ~5,600 tokens and warm-turn prefill is still only the new user text, while Hermes' decode degradation over 8-32K is modest for a dense model. Budget one slow turn (~8 s) whenever `chat_size` rolls the window — see risks.
memory_gb:
**Recommended (Hermes-4.3-36B-4bit): ~24 GB resident for the brain, leaving ~72-90 GB free.**

Arithmetic — weights = params x bits / 8:
- Hermes-4.3-36B: 4-bit mixed (6-bit embeddings/lm_head) ≈ **20.5 GB**; 5-bit ≈ 24 GB; 6-bit mixed ≈ **29 GB**; 8-bit ≈ 38 GB; bf16 = 72 GB. All fit.
- KV cache: Seed-OSS-36B is 64 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128 -> 2 x 64 x 8 x 128 x 2 B = 256 KB/token. At your ~6K working context = **1.5 GB**; at 32K = 8 GB. Halve with `--kv-bits 8`. So the total for the recommendation is ~22 GB weights + ~1.5 GB KV + ~1 GB runtime ≈ **24 GB**.

The rest of the shortlist, same arithmetic:
- gpt-oss-120b: native MXFP4 ≈ **63 GB**. KV ~72 KB/token full / ~36 KB effective under sliding window -> <0.6 GB at 8K. Fits with room.
- Qwen3.5-122B-A10B: 4-bit measured **69.6 GB** (bf16 would be 244 GB); 5-bit ~82 GB; 6.5-bit ~104 GB (marginal). KV is tiny (~24 KB/token — only ~12 of 48 layers are full attention) -> ~0.2 GB at 8K.
- MiniMax-M2.5 230B: 4-bit ≈ 115 GB (too tight), 3-bit ≈ **86 GB**.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash 284B: 8-bit = 284 GB ✗; 4-bit flat = 142 GB ✗; MXFP4 at 4.25 bpw = 151 GB ✗; real 3-bit ~3.3 bpw = 117 GB ✗ (above the practical wired limit); **2.44 bpw mixed = 92.8 GB disk / 84.4 GB measured peak ✓** — the only one that fits, and the slowest.

**Headroom accounting.** hw.memsize is 137438953472 B = 128 GiB. `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` is currently 0, i.e. macOS default of roughly 75% (~96 GB) wireable by the GPU; raise it to ~112 GB before running anything over 90 GB. Subtract the rest of the VoxEMW pipeline: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf bf16 ~1.2 GB + Qwen3-TTS-1.7B 6-bit MLX ~2 GB + Silero VAD ~0.5 GB + MiniCPM-V-4.6 Q4 sidecar ~2.7 GB ≈ **7 GB**, plus ~8-12 GB for macOS and the browser. So the realistic LLM budget is **~78-100 GB**, not 128 — which is exactly why the 4-bit DeepSeek-V4-Flash at 142 GB was never on the table and the 2.44-bit at 84 GB leaves almost nothing for the rest.

Key non-obvious point: **KV cache is a rounding error for every candidate** (all use MLA, GQA-with-2-KV-heads, Gated DeltaNet, or sliding-window). Weights dominate entirely; do not size the machine around context length.
install_commands: # 0. Raise the GPU wired-memory limit (default is ~75% of 128 GiB). Persist in /etc/sysctl.conf if you want it across reboots.
sudo sysctl -w iogpu.wired_limit_mb=114688
# 1. Dedicated venv for the brain, on 3.12 (VoxEMW's .venv-mac is also 3.12; do NOT use the homebrew 3.14 — MLX wheels lag).
uv venv --python 3.12 ~/.venvs/voxbrain
uv pip install --python ~/.venvs/voxbrain/bin/python 'mlx-lm>=0.28.3'
# 2. Primary brain: Hermes-4.3-36B 4-bit MLX (~21 GB). seed_oss is supported by mlx-lm 0.28.3+.
~/.venvs/voxbrain/bin/hf download leonsarmiento/Hermes-4.3-36B-4bit-mlx
# 3. Serve it OpenAI-compatible with the LRU prefix cache enabled (this is what makes warm TTFT ~0.1 s).
~/.venvs/voxbrain/bin/python -m mlx_lm server --model leonsarmiento/Hermes-4.3-36B-4bit-mlx --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --kv-bits 8

risks: **`chat_size: 30` will periodically destroy the prefix cache.** Once the rolling window starts dropping the oldest turns, the prompt gets SHORTER and the prefix after the system prompt shifts — that is the exact case mlx-lm issue #980 says cannot be trimmed for hybrid models, and even for full-attention Hermes it forces a re-prefill of everything after the drop point. Symptom: one turn in N stalls for several seconds with no other explanation. Mitigations, in order: raise chat_size so a normal debate session never rolls (60 messages ≈ 30 turns); or enable upstream's compact_history so summarisation happens at a controlled moment; or accept it and pre-warm again after each roll. Measure this before believing the latency estimate.

**The chat template must render byte-identically across turns or every cache hit is lost silently.** If the template strips <think> blocks from prior assistant turns, or re-orders anything when a message is appended, the trie lookup misses and you pay a full 8 s prefill with no error message. This is the single most likely reason the modelled latency fails in practice. Verify by logging prompt-token count vs prefilled-token count per request and asserting the delta stays ~40 tokens.

**Hermes-4.3-36B is dense, so it is the slowest decoder on the shortlist (~25 tok/s at 4-bit).** The 0.85 s LLM stage has less margin than the 122B MoE alternatives. If Qwen3-ASR comes in at the top of its measured 0.3-1.0 s range on a long utterance, or TTS TTFA drifts above 0.3 s, you can exceed 2.0 s. Keep the 35B-A3B insurance option ready, and instrument each stage separately rather than only measuring end to end.

**The 36B quality gap is real and untested for this job.** RefusalBench measures willingness to engage, not argument quality. Hermes-4.3-36B is claimed to roughly match Hermes 4 70B, but it is still ~3.4x fewer total params than Qwen3.5-122B. The specific failure to watch for is not refusal but shallowness: repeating the same three talking points by turn 10. Test with a scripted 20-turn adversarial debate before committing, and A/B against Qwen3.5-122B-A10B on the same transcript.

**mlx_lm.server is a reference server, not production infrastructure.** Known open bug #1292: it can return 1-token completions when a system prompt is reused with a different user prompt — i.e. exactly the partial-prefix-match case your voice loop hits on every single turn. This is reported on Qwen3.6 MTP variants specifically, but it is the same code path. Test for it explicitly (10 consecutive turns, same system prompt, different user text) and if it bites, switch the server to vmlx or vllm-mlx — the VoxEMW config does not change, only the process behind base_url.

**Prefix caching is stateful across concurrent sessions and VoxEMW has exactly one pipeline slot.** The orchestrator already kills old sessions when a new browser connects (num_pipelines: 1, 1008 close). If two personas or two sessions interleave, they will thrash the LRU cache against each other. Given the single-slot design this is low probability, but pin it: one persona per server process, and restart the server when switching personas rather than relying on the cache to sort itself out.

**The persona is built on a real, named public figure (project 'distillCKirk'), and the TTS stage is a zero-shot voice cloner fed a ref.wav.** A local debate-practice partner is a legitimate use, but a system that reproduces a specific real person's name, voice and positions is impersonation-shaped if it is ever shared, recorded, or published. Keep it local and single-user as designed; label the persona in-product as a practice opponent rather than the person; and do not clone the real individual's actual voice for anything that leaves the machine. This is a product/legal risk, not a model-selection one, but it sits on the same component.

**Abliterated / Heretic-decensored variants are a trap for this pipeline.** They are the obvious answer if a model refuses, and Heretic does score well (3/100 refusals on Gemma-3-12B, KL 0.16, better than manual abliteration's 0.45-1.04). But abliterated models are reported to be less stable on odd prompts, and in a live voice loop instability manifests as incoherent audio the user cannot interrupt or re-roll — strictly worse than a clean refusal you can detect and retry. Prefer a natively-permissive model (Hermes) over a surgically-modified one.

**oMLX / vMLX / vllm-mlx are all young third-party runtimes** with small maintainer counts, and two of them (oMLX for DeepSeek V4, vMLX for hybrid prefix caching) are load-bearing for the alternatives rather than the recommendation. The primary recommendation deliberately depends only on mainline mlx-lm for exactly this reason. If you take an alternative, you are also taking on that runtime's release risk in your critical path.

**Nothing is installed yet — torch, mlx and llama.cpp are all absent**, and VoxEMW's .venv-mac does not exist on this machine. The latency numbers above are modelled from published M5 Max benchmarks (the DeepSeek 2.4-bit card is measured on this exact chip; the hardware-corner table is measured on this exact chip; Hermes-36B is extrapolated from the Qwen3.5-27B anchor). Hermes-4.3-36B's decode and prefill rates on M5 Max are the one number in this report that nobody has published — measure it first, before building anything around it.
